title: 11 Bringing It Home Central Bank Gold Repatriation

concepts.title: Definition of Gold Repatriation
concepts.summary: Gold repatriation is the process where central banks move physical gold reserves from foreign custodians back to their own country's vault storage.
evidence_quotes: Gold repatriation refers to the process by which central banks move their physical gold reserves from the vaults of foreign gold custodians and back to vault storage within their own countries.

concepts.title: Drivers for Repatriation
concepts.summary: Several factors drive central banks to repatriate gold, including geopolitical tensions, sanctions risks, and the need for physical audits.
evidence_quotes: The impulse to bring gold back into central banks’ possession has been driven by several factors, including geopolitical tensions and sanctions risks, a desire for economic sovereignty, the need for physical audits, and the erosion of trust among the world’s central banks.

concepts.title: Erosion of Trust in Monetary Order
concepts.summary: The breakdown of trust in the international monetary order is evidenced by high gold purchases and the ongoing trend to repatriate reserves.
evidence_quotes: The breakdown of trust in the international monetary order is manifesting itself in the highest gold purchases by central banks since 1971 and the ongoing trend to repatriate gold reserves.

concepts.title: Mitigating Sanctions Risk
concepts.summary: Central banks repatriate gold to keep it under sovereign control to prevent it from being frozen or sanctioned by entities like the US, EU, and G7.
evidence_quotes: Mitigating sanctions risk: With the US, the EU, and the G7 active in imposing sanctions and freezing and confiscating foreign reserves, central banks repatriate gold and keep it under sovereign control to prevent it from becoming frozen or sanctioned.

concepts.title: Auditing Requirements
concepts.summary: Central banks are compelled to repatriate gold to satisfy demands for physical audits from federal auditors.
evidence_quotes: Auditing: Some federal auditors have demanded physical gold audits. Since the New York Federal Reserve and Bank of England custodians prohibit physical audits, central banks are compelled to repatriate gold to be physically audited and verified.

concepts.title: Concentration Risk in Storage
concepts.summary: State auditors can direct central banks to repatriate gold to diversify storage and reduce concentration risk from holding too much in one foreign vault.
evidence_quotes: Concentration risk: State auditors can deem that holding a high percentage of central bank gold in a single foreign vault poses a concentration risk and can direct the central bank to repatriate gold to diversify its storage and reduce concentration risk.

concepts.title: Geopolitical Tensions Motivation
concepts.summary: Rising political and military conflicts motivate central banks to move gold reserves to domestic storage to reduce exposure to international conflicts.
evidence_quotes: Geopolitical tensions: Rising political and military conflicts, potential trade wars, and trade bloc realignments motivate central banks to move gold reserves to domestic storage to reduce exposure to international conflicts and asset freezes.

concepts.title: Counterparty Risk Re-evaluation
concepts.summary: The importance of unencumbered gold is reinforced as central banks re-evaluate counterparty risk following financial crises.
evidence_quotes: Counterparty risk: Physical gold has no counterparty risk, but this is only fully true when the gold is stored domestically rather than deposited abroad.

concepts.title: Strategic Reserve Asset Value
concepts.summary: Gold is considered a strategic asset with rising value, and its safest storage is domestically, free from external control.
evidence_quotes: A strategic reserve asset: Gold is a central bank’s most strategic asset, with a rising value and the foundation of national wealth.

concepts.title: Confidence-Building Measure
concepts.summary: Repatriating gold strengthens national sovereignty and boosts public trust as a confidence-building measure.
evidence_quotes: A confidence-building measure: Repatriating gold strengthens national sovereignty and boosts public trust.

concepts.title: Practical Reasons for Foreign Storage
concepts.summary: Practical reasons for storing gold with third-party custodians include security, liquidity, and market access.
evidence_quotes: Security and physical safety: These institutions are known for their highly secure vaults with advanced physical and surveillance security, and they have long-standing experience storing the gold reserves of many central banks.

concepts.title: Security and Physical Safety
concepts.summary: Institutions like the Bank of England offer highly secure vaults with advanced security for gold storage.
evidence_quotes: Security and physical safety: These institutions are known for their highly secure vaults with advanced physical and surveillance security, and they have long-standing experience storing the gold reserves of many central banks.

concepts.title: Liquidity and Market Access

concepts.title: Diversification of Storage Risk
